name: bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data that owns bfqq, bfqq is the queue being expired (normally the in-service queue), compensate says whether the idle time is excluded from the measured service time, reason is a bfqq_expiration value; the caller is expected to hold bfqd->lock (this function itself takes and releases no lock and takes or drops no reference directly). Postcondition: returns nothing. (1) slow = bfq_bfqq_is_slow(bfqd, bfqq, compensate, &delta) with delta (milliseconds) initialised to 0. For a non-sync bfqq bfq_bfqq_is_slow returns false at once and delta stays 0. For a sync bfqq it writes delta in each of its cases: BFQ_MIN_TT/NSEC_PER_MSEC (non-rotational device) or bfq_slice_idle/NSEC_PER_MSEC (rotational device) when the measured interval is under 1000 microseconds (slow is then BFQQ_SEEKY(bfqq)), otherwise the interval in milliseconds, with slow = (bfqq->entity.service < bfq_max_budget/2) when the interval exceeds 20000 microseconds and slow = BFQQ_SEEKY(bfqq) when it is between 1000 and 20000 microseconds. The interval runs from bfqd->last_budget_start to bfqd->last_idling_start when compensate is true, otherwise to the current time. (2) Only if bfqq->wr_coeff == 1 and (slow, or reason == BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT with bfq_bfqq_budget_left(bfqq) >= entity->budget/3) it calls bfq_bfqq_charge_time(bfqd, bfqq, delta) (delta is 0 for a non-sync queue). (3) If bfqd->low_latency and wr_coeff == 1, last_wr_start_finish = jiffies. (4) If bfqd->low_latency, bfqd->bfq_wr_max_softrt_rate > 0 and bfqq->sort_list is empty: dispatched == 0 sets soft_rt_next_start = bfq_bfqq_softrt_next_start(bfqd, bfqq); dispatched > 0 marks the softrt_update flag; a negative dispatched does neither. (5) bfqd->rqs_injected and bfqd->wait_dispatch are set to false and bfqd->waited_rq to NULL. (6) __bfq_bfqq_recalc_budget(bfqd, bfqq, reason) is called, then __bfq_bfqq_expire(bfqd, bfqq, reason) (which may set the split_coop mark, removes bfqq from the busy structures or requeues it, and may free bfqq). If that returns true (bfqq is gone) the function returns immediately without touching any service field. Otherwise: if bfqq is not busy and reason is neither BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT nor BFQQE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, bfqq is marked non_blocking_wait_rq and bfqq->entity.service is left unchanged; in the else case bfqq->entity.service is set to 0. Finally entity = entity->parent and entity->service = 0 is applied to each entity of the for_each_entity loop starting there: with CONFIG_BFQ_GROUP_IOSCHED every ancestor up the parent chain until a NULL parent, without it at most the single entity->parent if it is non-NULL. The only return statements are the early return after __bfq_bfqq_expire returns true and the implicit return at the end of the function.
note: Reviewer claim 1 (non-sync queues can still be slow via BFQQ_SEEKY): WRONG. block/bfq-iosched.c:4154 initialises slow = BFQQ_SEEKY but 4156-4157 'if (!bfq_bfqq_sync(bfqq)) return false;' returns false before any use, so for a non-sync queue slow is false and *delta_ms is never written (delta keeps its initial 0 from 4340). Reviewer claim 2 (delta set only when compensate and interval >= 1ms): WRONG. For a sync queue delta is written on both sides of the 1 ms test (4173/4175 for interval < 1000 us, 4180 otherwise); 'compensate' only selects the interval end (4159-4162). Other fixes made: the parent-entity loop (4449-4451) description now states exactly what for_each_entity does in each config (bfq-iosched.h:1105-1106 and 1123-1124), earlier 'single level otherwise' was inexact; slow definition now spells out the three interval ranges (4167-4198); softrt branch handles dispatched<0 explicitly (4386-4395).

name: _badblocks_set
prose: Precondition: bb points to an initialised struct badblocks with a valid page table; the caller does not hold bb->lock (the function takes the write seqlock itself, saving interrupt flags); [s, s+sectors) is the range to record and acknowledged says whether the new entries are acknowledged. Postcondition: the function has these exits. (a) If bb->shift < 0 (badblocks disabled) it returns false at once, taking no lock and changing nothing. (b) If sectors == 0 it returns false at once, taking no lock and changing nothing. (c) Otherwise, if bb->shift != 0, the code evaluates rounddown(s, 1 << bb->shift) and roundup(next, 1 << bb->shift) but these macros are statement expressions that return a value and do not assign to their argument, and the results are discarded, so s and next are unchanged and sectors = next - s keeps its original value: no rounding to the shift granularity takes place. Then it takes the write seqlock (irq-saving) and loops over re_insert. Each pass sets bad.start = s, bad.len = sectors and handles one piece of the range: if the table is full (badblocks_full) it jumps to out without inserting; if the table is empty it inserts the whole piece at index 0 (count + 1); otherwise it finds prev = prev_badblocks and (i) with no entry starting at or before s it inserts at index 0, trimming the piece to end before the first existing entry (count + 1); (ii) if can_combine_front, it combines p[prev-1] with p[prev] (count - 1, added); (iii) else if can_merge_front it merges into p[prev]; (iv) else if the piece overlaps p[prev], then if can_front_overwrite fails with extra > 0 (extra table slots needed) it jumps to out, and if it fails with extra <= 0 it skips min(BB_END(p[prev]) - s, sectors) sectors without changing the table, while if it succeeds it overwrites in front (count increased by extra, added) and then combines with the previous entry when possible (count - 1); (v) otherwise it inserts after prev, trimmed to end before the next entry if it overlaps that one (count + 1). After a piece, s advances and sectors decreases by the length handled; if sectors is still above 0 the loop repeats, else try_adjacent_combine(bb, prev) is called (it may merge p[prev] with p[prev+1] and decrement count; its result is ignored) and control reaches out. At out, if added != 0, set_changed(bb) is called and then, if acknowledged is 0, bb->unacked_exist = 1, else badblocks_update_acked(bb). The write seqlock is released with the saved flags and the function returns (sectors == 0), i.e. true exactly when the whole range was processed (recorded or skipped over), false when it stopped early at out because the table was full or an overwrite needed extra slots; in the early-stop case the part of the range handled before the stop stays recorded. The write seqlock is taken once and released once, at the exit after out.
note: Reviewer claim (rounddown/roundup mutate s and next so the range is rounded): WRONG. block/badblocks.c:860-861 are the calls 'rounddown(s, 1 << bb->shift); roundup(next, 1 << bb->shift);' as bare statements; include/linux/math.h:71-76 defines roundup(x,y) as a statement expression '({ typeof(y) __y = y; (((x) + (__y - 1)) / __y) * __y; })' and math.h:85-90 defines rounddown(x,y) as '({ typeof(x) __x = (x); __x - (__x % (y)); })'; both only compute a value, neither assigns to x, so s and next are not modified and line 862 'sectors = next - s' equals the original sectors. (This is a known upstream quirk of this version; the same pattern is at badblocks.c:1074-1075 and 1310-1311.) Prose now spells out the rounding no-op and enumerates all exits and each branch's count effect from the source (badblocks.c:866-980).

name: btrfs_replace_file_extents
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inode lock and has locked the file range [start, end] (end inclusive); path is a usable empty path in the inode's root; extent_info is NULL (hole punch) or describes the replacement extent; trans_out is a valid output pointer. Return statements: there are exactly two. (R1) If end <= start the function returns -EINVAL at the very top, before initialising the temporary reservation; nothing is changed. (R2) All the other paths, listed below, end at out_release, which releases the temporary block reservation rsv (btrfs_block_rsv_release of all of it) and returns ret. Before that: the function initialises rsv (a stack-allocated temporary reservation, failfast) and starts a transaction with 3 reserved items, or 2 when the NO_HOLES incompat feature is set and extent_info is NULL. Goto/exit structure: (a) btrfs_start_transaction fails: ret = its error, trans = NULL, goto out_release (no transaction to end, no full-sync flag set). (b) btrfs_block_rsv_migrate fails (WARN_ON): goto out_trans with the live transaction, which is ended with btrfs_end_transaction (no abort, no full-sync flag). Then the loop `while (cur_offset < end)` runs with trans->block_rsv = &rsv; each pass calls btrfs_drop_extents for [cur_offset, end+1); if extent_info is NULL the inode's byte count is reduced by drop_args.bytes_found after every call, whatever its result. If the drop result is anything other than -ENOSPC, including 0, the loop is left with ret equal to that result; the transaction is aborted (btrfs_abort_transaction) when ret is non-zero unless ret is -EOPNOTSUPP and not (extent_info non-NULL with is_new_extent). So the loop repeats only after a drop that returned -ENOSPC (it does not repeat after a successful drop, because a successful drop breaks out and the remainder is handled after the loop). In an -ENOSPC pass: trans->block_rsv is switched to the fs trans_block_rsv; with extent_info NULL the dropped part [cur_offset, drop_end) is filled with hole items by fill_holes when cur_offset < i_size rounded up to the sector size, else (cur_offset < drop_end only) cleared from the file extent range map with btrfs_inode_clear_file_extent_range; each of those failing aborts the transaction and leaves the loop. With extent_info non-NULL and drop_end > extent_info->file_offset, btrfs_insert_replace_extent inserts the piece up to drop_end (failure aborts and leaves the loop) and data_len, data_offset and file_offset are advanced by that piece. Then i_version is bumped, mtime and ctime are set when extent_info is NULL or extent_info->update_times, and btrfs_update_inode is called (failure aborts and leaves the loop). The transaction is ended (btrfs_end_transaction, then btrfs_btree_balance_dirty) and a new one with the same item count is started; a failure of btrfs_start_transaction there sets ret to its error, trans = NULL and leaves the loop (no abort); a failing btrfs_block_rsv_migrate (WARN_ON) leaves the loop with the live transaction (no abort). Otherwise trans->block_rsv = &rsv, cur_offset = drop_end, len = end - cur_offset, and if extent_info is NULL and len is non-zero find_first_non_hole may advance cur_offset and len past a hole: a negative result leaves the loop (no abort), a positive result with len == 0 sets ret = 0 and leaves the loop, a positive result with len > 0 continues the loop. After the loop: if extent_info is non-NULL and not is_new_extent the inode is flagged for a full fsync (btrfs_set_inode_full_sync), even if ret is non-zero; this flag is not set on the paths (a) and (b) above. If ret is non-zero control goes to out_trans. Otherwise: if drop_end <= end then drop_end = end + 1; with extent_info NULL, [cur_offset, drop_end) is filled with holes when cur_offset < rounded-up i_size and cur_offset < drop_end, else cleared from the extent range map when cur_offset < drop_end; with extent_info non-NULL the remainder of the replacement extent (data_len) is inserted with btrfs_insert_replace_extent; each of these steps aborts the transaction on failure and goes to out_trans. out_trans: if trans is NULL go to out_release; otherwise trans->block_rsv = &fs_info->trans_block_rsv, then if ret is non-zero btrfs_end_transaction(trans) (its result is ignored, *trans_out untouched), else *trans_out = trans and the live transaction is left for the caller to end. The function returns 0 on success or a negative errno (from starting a transaction, migrating the reservation, dropping extents, filling holes, clearing the range, inserting the replacement extent, updating the inode or find_first_non_hole).
note: Reviewer claim (the loop repeats after a successful drop as well, not only on -ENOSPC): WRONG. fs/btrfs/file.c:2407-2426: after btrfs_drop_extents, 'if (ret != -ENOSPC) { ...; break; }' is taken for ret == 0 as well as for every other error, so a successful drop leaves the loop; only -ENOSPC reaches the code at 2428-2532 and loops again. (The unconditional 'break' at 2425 is inside the ret != -ENOSPC branch whose abort test at 2421-2424 only fires for ret != 0.) The success-case remainder is handled after the loop at 2559-2593. Additional precision added from the source: byte-count update happens every call regardless of result (2409-2411); the abort condition for -EOPNOTSUPP (2421-2423); the positive-ret handling of find_first_non_hole (2524-2531, 2142-2163); the exact two return statements (2371, 2606); full-sync flag not set on paths (a)/(b) (2392, 2398 jump past 2541).

name: BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64)
prose: The macro invocation BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64) (accessors.h:265, macro defined at accessors.h:62-74) generates two static inline functions, each starting with a compile-time check that the member is exactly 64 bits wide: u64 btrfs_inode_size(const struct extent_buffer *eb, const struct btrfs_inode_item *s) and void btrfs_set_inode_size(const struct extent_buffer *eb, struct btrfs_inode_item *s, u64 val). Precondition: eb is a valid extent buffer and s is the offset of an inode item inside eb, represented as a pointer value (not a dereferenceable address). Postcondition, getter: it has a single return statement, return btrfs_get_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size)). With member_offset = (unsigned long)s + offsetof(size): if member_offset + 8 > eb->len, btrfs_get_64 issues a btrfs_warn bounds report and returns 0; otherwise it returns the 64-bit little-endian value stored at that offset (read across two folios when the field straddles a folio boundary). The getter does not modify the buffer. Postcondition, setter: it returns nothing and calls btrfs_set_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size), val). If member_offset + 8 > eb->len it issues the same bounds warning and writes nothing; otherwise it stores val in little-endian byte order at that offset (split across two folios when the field straddles a boundary), which modifies the extent buffer contents (the const qualifier on eb applies to the descriptor, not the data). Neither function takes a lock, takes or drops a reference, allocates memory or marks the buffer dirty.
note: Previously unreviewed (the review call failed), prose re-derived from fs/btrfs/accessors.h:62-74 (macro) and fs/btrfs/accessors.c:51-112 (DEFINE_BTRFS_SETGET_BITS: bounds check at 63-66 for get, 93-96 for set; split-folio paths 71-80 and 102-111). Wording tightened: bounds condition stated exactly (member_offset + 8 > eb->len), both single exits enumerated, no 'always/never' claims.

name: btrfs_init_new_device
prose: Function btrfs_init_new_device(fs_info, device_path) (volumes.c:2801; the slice starts at its line 2841, after the open and size checks): adds the block device at device_path as a new writeable device of the mounted filesystem. Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem; the caller holds none of the locks the function takes (sb->s_umount, uuid_mutex, fs_devices->device_list_mutex, fs_info->chunk_mutex); the function may sleep. Steps and exits in order. Before the slice: -EROFS is returned if the superblock is read-only and fs_devices->seeding is not set; the error of bdev_file_open_by_path (BLK_OPEN_WRITE, fs_holder_ops) is returned if the open fails; if btrfs_check_device_zone_type fails or the device size is <= BTRFS_DEVICE_RANGE_RESERVED, ret = -EINVAL and the path goes to label error (bdev_fput, no locks held yet). In the slice: if fs_devices->seeding is set, seeding_dev = true, sb->s_umount is taken for writing and then uuid_mutex, locked = true; these are held until after the first transaction commit (or released at label error). sync_blockdev is called. If a device in fs_devices->devices already uses the same block device, ret = -EEXIST and goto error. btrfs_alloc_device failure: ret = its error, goto error. Otherwise the new device's bdev_file, bdev and fs_info are set; lookup_bdev failure or btrfs_get_dev_zone_info failure: goto error_free_device (btrfs_free_device, then error). btrfs_start_transaction(dev_root, 0) failure: goto error_free_zone (destroy zone info, free device, error). Label error does bdev_fput and, if locked, releases uuid_mutex then s_umount, and returns ret. After a transaction exists, the device fields are initialised (writeable, in-fs-metadata, io_width/io_align/sector_size = sectorsize, total_bytes = disk size rounded down to the sector size, blocksize set). If seeding_dev, btrfs_init_sprout(fs_info) is called with neither device_list_mutex nor chunk_mutex held (it allocates); on error the transaction is aborted and goto error_trans (end the transaction, then error_free_zone, error_free_device, error). Then device_list_mutex is taken; for seeding btrfs_setup_sprout and btrfs_assign_next_active_device run under device_list_mutex only (chunk_mutex is not yet held); device->fs_devices is set; chunk_mutex is taken and only under it the device is added to fs_devices->devices and alloc_list, num_devices, open_devices, rw_devices and total_devices are incremented, total_rw_bytes and free_chunk_space grow by the device size, rotating is set if the device is rotational, the super block total bytes (rounded down to the sector size) and num_devices (+1) are updated (the original values saved in orig_super_total_bytes and orig_super_num_devices) and btrfs_clear_space_info_full is called; chunk_mutex is released; btrfs_sysfs_add_device(device) runs after chunk_mutex is released while device_list_mutex is still held; then device_list_mutex is released. If seeding_dev, init_first_rw_device runs under chunk_mutex; on error the transaction is aborted and goto error_sysfs. Then btrfs_add_dev_item (error: abort transaction, goto error_sysfs); for seeding btrfs_finish_sprout (error: abort, goto error_sysfs) and btrfs_sysfs_update_sprout_fsid. Then ret = btrfs_commit_transaction(trans). Seeding case: uuid_mutex and s_umount are released (locked = false) right after that commit; if the commit returned non-zero its error is returned at once (no rollback, no forget, no time update); otherwise btrfs_relocate_sys_chunks runs (a negative result is only reported through btrfs_handle_fs_error and does not change the return value), then btrfs_attach_transaction: -ENOENT means return 0 immediately (no forget, no time update); another error sets ret and trans = NULL and goes to error_sysfs; success makes ret the result of a second btrfs_commit_transaction. Then (non-seeding after the first commit, seeding after the second) btrfs_forget_devices(device->devt) (result ignored) and update_dev_time(device_path) run and the function returns ret, which is 0 on success or the commit error (the commit error is not rolled back). Rollback at error_sysfs: btrfs_sysfs_remove_device, device_list_mutex taken, for seeding btrfs_assign_next_active_device(device, seed_devices->latest_dev), chunk_mutex taken, the device is taken off post_commit_list if on it and off dev_list and alloc_list, num_devices, open_devices, rw_devices and total_devices are decremented, total_rw_bytes and free_chunk_space are reduced by the device size, the super block total bytes and num_devices are restored to the saved values, both mutexes are released; then it continues through error_trans (btrfs_end_transaction if trans is non-NULL), error_free_zone, error_free_device and error (bdev_fput, release uuid_mutex and s_umount only if locked is still true) and returns ret. Rollback does not undo fs_devices->rotating, the space-info full flags, or the sprout setup. There are six return statements: -EROFS, the open error, the seeding first-commit error, 0 for -ENOENT from btrfs_attach_transaction, the normal return of ret, and the return of ret at the end of the error labels.
note: Reviewer claim (prose said sprout and sysfs add happen under chunk_mutex; code does them outside it): RIGHT. fs/btrfs/volumes.c:2893 btrfs_init_sprout runs before any mutex is taken (comment at 2892 'GFP_KERNEL allocation must not be under device_list_mutex'); 2901-2906 btrfs_setup_sprout/btrfs_assign_next_active_device run under device_list_mutex only (chunk_mutex is taken at 2910); 2939 chunk_mutex is unlocked before 2942 btrfs_sysfs_add_device, which still runs under device_list_mutex (released at 2944). The previous prose put the sprout and sysfs add under both mutexes: that was a real error and is fixed. Also re-checked every return/goto: returns at 2817, 2822, 2984, 2993, 3013, 3050; labels 3015-3049; rollback restores counters at 3025-3034 and does not undo rotating (2921-2922) or btrfs_clear_space_info_full (2937).

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: btrfs_commit_transaction(trans) starts at line 2209 of transaction.c; this slice (ending at line 2284) shows its beginning and stops in the middle of the branch taken when another task is already committing, the rest of the function (lines 2285-2646) being in the next slice. Precondition: trans is a transaction handle of trans->fs_info, cur_trans = trans->transaction, trans->use_count is 1 (checked only by ASSERT); the handle is consumed by each of the exits of the whole function (ended with btrfs_end_transaction, or freed after the commit, or freed in the cleanup path), so the caller must not use it afterwards. Behaviour of the part shown. The function first clears BTRFS_FS_NEED_TRANS_COMMIT. (1) If TRANS_ABORTED(cur_trans), ret = cur_trans->aborted and control goes to label lockdep_trans_commit_start_release, which ends the handle with btrfs_end_transaction (its result ignored) and returns ret; no further step is done. (2) Otherwise btrfs_trans_release_metadata(trans) is called and trans->block_rsv = NULL. If this task is the one that sets BTRFS_DELAYED_REFS_FLUSHING (test_and_set_bit), btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, 0) runs and a non-zero result goes to the same label (handle ended, that errno returned) before btrfs_create_pending_block_groups is called. Then btrfs_create_pending_block_groups(trans) is called (no result). If BTRFS_TRANS_DIRTY_BG_RUN is not yet set, under ro_block_group_mutex the task tries to set it and only the task that set it calls btrfs_start_dirty_block_groups(trans); a non-zero result goes to the same label (handle ended, that errno returned). (3) Under fs_info->trans_lock: if cur_trans->state is already at least TRANS_STATE_COMMIT_PREP (another task is committing), the local want_state is initialised to TRANS_STATE_COMPLETED and add_pending_snapshot(trans) links trans->pending_snapshot (when non-NULL) into cur_trans->pending_snapshots; trans_lock is released and cur_trans->use_count is incremented; the following lines, after the end of this slice (2285-2298), change want_state to TRANS_STATE_SUPER_COMMITTED if trans->in_fsync, release the COMMIT_PREP lockdep map, set ret = btrfs_end_transaction(trans), call wait_for_commit(cur_trans, want_state), replace ret by cur_trans->aborted if the transaction is aborted, drop the extra reference and return ret. So the want_state value is COMPLETED at the end of this slice and is overridden to SUPER_COMMITTED two lines later when trans->in_fsync is set. If the state is below COMMIT_PREP (trans_lock still held), this task performs the commit as described for the next slice. Within this slice there is no return statement; the only exit in the shown part is the jump to lockdep_trans_commit_start_release described above (the 'return ret' at 2645), plus the branch exit continuing after the slice. The pending snapshot of trans is not linked on the exits in (1) and (2).
note: Reviewer claim (annotation says want_state becomes SUPER_COMMITTED when trans->in_fsync but code sets COMPLETED unconditionally): the slice ends at line 2284, so the reviewer saw only the initialiser transaction.c:2278 'enum btrfs_trans_state want_state = TRANS_STATE_COMPLETED;' and not the override at transaction.c:2285-2286 'if (trans->in_fsync) want_state = TRANS_STATE_SUPER_COMMITTED;' (also 2306-2309 for the previous-transaction wait), so the original annotation is right about the function but not about the visible slice; the prose now says explicitly which part is in the slice (COMPLETED at 2278) and that the override follows at 2285-2286. Re-checked early exits: 2222-2225 (aborted) and 2240-2242, 2270-2272 go to 2642-2645 (end handle, return ret).

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: This slice starts inside btrfs_commit_transaction (function at transaction.c:2209-2646) at line 2285, in the branch taken when another task is already committing, and ends at line 2540 inside the commit proper; the lines after 2540 are described last. Precondition: trans is a handle of trans->fs_info with trans->use_count 1 (ASSERT only), cur_trans = trans->transaction; the handle is consumed by each exit of the whole function (ended with btrfs_end_transaction, or freed after the commit, or freed in the cleanup path). Four return statements exist in the whole function: 2298 (waiting branch), 2616 (successful commit), 2635 (cleanup path) and 2645 (early exits). Behaviour. (A) Waiting branch, lines 2285-2299 (taken when cur_trans->state >= COMMIT_PREP, with want_state initialised to COMPLETED at 2278): want_state = SUPER_COMMITTED if trans->in_fsync, otherwise it stays COMPLETED; the COMMIT_PREP lockdep map is released; ret = btrfs_end_transaction(trans); wait_for_commit(cur_trans, want_state); if the transaction is aborted ret is replaced by cur_trans->aborted; the extra reference on cur_trans is dropped; it returns ret. (B) Commit proper, otherwise: state = COMMIT_PREP and waiters are woken. If cur_trans is not first in fs_info->trans_list, want_state = COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED if trans->in_fsync); if the previous transaction's state is below want_state, a reference on it is taken, trans_lock is dropped, wait_for_commit(prev_trans, want_state), ret = prev_trans->aborted, the reference is put, and a non-zero ret goes to label lockdep_release; otherwise trans_lock is retaken. If cur_trans is first in the list and BTRFS_FS_ERROR is set, trans_lock is dropped and ret = -EROFS goes to lockdep_release. The state becomes COMMIT_START, trans_lock is dropped, critical_section_start_time is recorded and the external-writer count is decremented. ret = btrfs_start_delalloc_flush(fs_info) (in this tree it only starts writeback when FLUSHONCOMMIT is set and returns 0, but the result is checked): non-zero goes to lockdep_release. ret = btrfs_run_delayed_items(trans): non-zero goes to lockdep_release. The label lockdep_release (2637-2640) only releases the extwriters and writers lockdep maps and then goes to cleanup_transaction, so these three failures end in the full cleanup path described below. Then the task waits until the external writer count is 0, runs btrfs_run_delayed_items a second time (non-zero: releases the writers lockdep map and goes directly to cleanup_transaction), calls btrfs_wait_delalloc_flush (waits only when FLUSHONCOMMIT is set), waits until pending_ordered is 0, calls btrfs_scrub_pause, then under trans_lock calls add_pending_snapshot(trans) and sets state COMMIT_DOING, waits until num_writers == 1, clears BTRFS_FS_COMMIT_TRANS, and if the transaction is aborted sets ret = cur_trans->aborted and goes to scrub_continue. Then it takes reloc_mutex and runs create_pending_snapshots, btrfs_run_delayed_items, btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, U64_MAX), commit_fs_roots, btrfs_free_log_root_tree, btrfs_qgroup_account_extents (a negative result fails) and commit_cowonly_roots; any non-zero (negative for qgroup) result goes to unlock_reloc with ret set; if the transaction is aborted after that, ret = cur_trans->aborted and the path goes to unlock_reloc. It then sets cur_trans = fs_info->running_transaction, adds the tree root and chunk root to cur_trans->switch_commits, calls switch_commit_roots and update_super_roots, zeroes the super block log root and level, copies super_copy to super_for_commit, calls btrfs_commit_device_sizes, clears BTRFS_FS_LOG1_ERR and LOG2_ERR, calls btrfs_trans_release_chunk_metadata and takes tree_log_mutex (line 2539; the slice ends here). After the slice: under trans_lock state = UNBLOCKED and fs_info->running_transaction = NULL; reloc_mutex is released; btrfs_write_and_wait_transaction (failure: btrfs_handle_fs_error, tree_log_mutex released, goto scrub_continue); write_all_supers(fs_info, 0) followed by releasing tree_log_mutex (failure: goto scrub_continue, without btrfs_handle_fs_error); update_commit_stats; state SUPER_COMMITTED; btrfs_finish_extent_commit (failure: goto scrub_continue); btrfs_clear_space_info_full if HAVE_FREE_BGS; btrfs_set_last_trans_committed; state COMPLETED; the transaction is removed from fs_info->trans_list; two references on cur_trans are dropped; sb_end_intwrite if the handle is freezable; btrfs_scrub_continue; current->journal_info is cleared if it is trans; the handle is freed; it returns ret (0 at that point). Labels: unlock_reloc releases reloc_mutex and falls into scrub_continue, which calls btrfs_scrub_continue and falls into cleanup_transaction: btrfs_trans_release_metadata, btrfs_cleanup_pending_block_groups, btrfs_trans_release_chunk_metadata, trans->block_rsv = NULL, a warning 'Skipping commit of aborted transaction.', current->journal_info cleared if it is trans, then cleanup_transaction(trans, ret) (aborts the transaction with ret, removes it from the transaction list, runs btrfs_cleanup_one_transaction, clears fs_info->running_transaction if it is this transaction, drops two references, cancels scrub unless relocation is running, and frees the handle); it returns the negative errno ret. lockdep_release releases two lockdep maps then goes to cleanup_transaction (so scrub is not resumed on that path, which is correct because scrub_pause has not yet run there). The pending snapshot of trans is linked into cur_trans->pending_snapshots only by the two add_pending_snapshot calls (2280 in the waiting branch and 2393 before COMMIT_DOING): not on the early exits, and not on failures before 2393 (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delalloc flush, first or second delayed items).

So those failures do end in the cleanup path (2625-2635), only through the lockdep_release label. The prose now names the label and states that it falls into cleanup_transaction. The second delayed-items failure (2369-2373) jumps directly to cleanup_transaction after one lockdep release. Verified all four returns (2298, 2616, 2635, 2645) and the scrub_continue/unlock_reloc fall-through ordering (2618-2635).

name: aio_poll_wake
prose: Function aio_poll_wake(wait, mode, sync, key) (aio.c:1787-1867), the wake callback of the wait-queue entry embedded in a poll_iocb. Precondition: wait is the wait entry of the poll_iocb of a live aio_kiocb (iocb = container_of, ki_ctx valid); the caller (the waitqueue wake-up code) holds the wait queue head's lock; key is the poll key, converted with key_to_poll (a NULL key gives mask 0); mode and sync are unused. Exits: there are two return statements. (R1) If mask is non-zero and mask & req->events is 0 the function returns 0 and changes nothing. (R2) Otherwise it returns 1 after branch A or branch B. Branch A, taken when mask != 0 and req->work_scheduled is false and spin_trylock_irqsave(&ki_ctx->ctx_lock) succeeds: the wait entry is removed from the wait queue (list_del_init), the iocb is removed from the context's active list (list_del(&iocb->ki_list)), ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask); if iocb->ki_eventfd is set and eventfd_signal_allowed() is false, the local iocb pointer is set to NULL and req->work is re-initialised as aio_poll_put_work and scheduled (the iocb_put is then done by that work); ctx_lock is released with the saved flags; and if the local pointer is still set, iocb_put(iocb) is called after the lock is released. Branch B, taken otherwise (mask == 0, or work already scheduled, or the trylock failed): the wait entry stays on the queue unless POLLFREE is set; if req->work_scheduled is already true, req->work_need_resched = true, else schedule_work(&req->work) and req->work_scheduled = true; then, if (mask & POLLFREE), req->cancelled is set, the wait entry is removed from the queue (list_del_init) and, as the last step, req->head is set to NULL with smp_store_release. Branch B does not take ctx_lock and does not drop an iocb reference. POLLFREE is only handled specially in branch B; if branch A is taken for a mask containing POLLFREE the request is completed inline as for any other mask. No lock is held on return except the caller's own wait queue lock (the function acquires and releases ctx_lock only inside branch A).
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:1787-1867 and aio_poll_put_work at aio.c:1671-1677, key_to_poll at include/linux/wait.h:237 (NULL key gives 0). Changes from previous prose: the inline-branch condition now lists exactly 'mask && !req->work_scheduled && trylock' (1812-1813), both list removals are named (1816-1817), the two returns are named (1797, 1866), and the POLLFREE sentence is restricted to branch B (1853-1864) without 'always/never' wording.

name: aio_poll
prose: Function aio_poll(aiocb, iocb) (aio.c:1894-1967) starts an IOCB_CMD_POLL request. Precondition: aiocb is an initialised aio_kiocb (ki_ctx valid; the poll request's file pointer, which shares storage with ki_filp, is set); iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block; the caller holds no ctx_lock. Return statements: three. (R1) -EINVAL, before the poll request is touched, if (u16)iocb->aio_buf != iocb->aio_buf. (R2) -EINVAL, likewise, if aio_offset, aio_nbytes or aio_rw_flags is non-zero. (R3) the final 'return apt.error' (value 0 or -EINVAL). Otherwise: the work item is initialised to aio_poll_complete_work, req->events = demangle_poll(aio_buf) | EPOLLERR | EPOLLHUP, head is NULL, cancelled, work_scheduled and work_need_resched are false, the wait entry is initialised with aio_poll_wake, and apt.error starts as -EINVAL, apt.queued false. mask = vfs_poll(file, &apt.pt) & req->events (the queue callback adds the wait entry to the file's wait queue on its first call and records head, queued = true and error = 0; a second call leaves error = -EINVAL). Then ctx->ctx_lock is taken with interrupts disabled. Case 1, apt.queued false (the file registered no wait queue): the lock is dropped; if mask != 0, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), apt.error = 0 and iocb_put(aiocb) is called after the lock is released and the function returns 0 (completed synchronously); if mask == 0 it returns -EINVAL (the request is not queued anywhere and the caller keeps the reference and must destroy it). Case 2, apt.queued true: on_queue = poll_iocb_lock_wq(req), which is true only if req->head is non-NULL and the wait entry is still linked, in which case the wait queue head lock (and RCU read lock) is then held. If !on_queue or req->work_scheduled (aio_poll_wake already completed it or scheduled the completion work): if apt.error was non-zero (the file registered more than one wait queue) cancel is set; then apt.error = 0 and mask = 0. Next, if mask != 0 or apt.error != 0 (this can then only hold while on_queue is true and no work is scheduled): the wait entry is removed from the queue; else if cancel: req->cancelled is set (the iocb is not added to active_reqs); else if on_queue: the iocb is added to ctx->active_reqs and ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel; else nothing more is done. If on_queue the wait queue lock is released. After that, if mask != 0 (synchronous completion; the request is no longer on a wait queue, or was not on one to begin with): ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask) and apt.error = 0. ctx_lock is released; if mask != 0 iocb_put(aiocb) is called; the function returns apt.error. Result summary of case 2: it returns 0 when the request was completed synchronously (mask != 0 with no work scheduled and still on the queue), when it is waiting for an event (on the queue, no work scheduled, mask 0, one wait queue; now on active_reqs), when completion was already done or scheduled by aio_poll_wake (any mask ignored), and when more than one wait queue was registered but aio_poll_wake had already run (cancelled set); it returns -EINVAL when more than one wait queue was registered and the request was still on its first queue with no work scheduled and no event ready (the wait entry has been removed and the caller keeps the iocb reference), and it completes synchronously with return 0 when more than one wait queue was registered, the request was still on its queue with no work scheduled and mask != 0. ctx_lock and the wait queue lock are not held on any return.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived by enumerating every branch of aio.c:1894-1967 (returns at 1904, 1907, 1966; cases 1929-1958 and 1959-1965). Cross-checked: poll_iocb_lock_wq at aio.c:1695-1716 returns true only with head lock and RCU held (1707-1711); aio_poll_queue_proc at 1876-1892 sets queued/error; the earlier prose omitted the case where, with multiple wait queues and mask != 0 on an on-queue request, the request is completed synchronously (the 'mask || apt.error' branch at 1942 followed by 1959-1962). Language 'always/never' avoided; all exceptions listed.

name: __io_submit_one
prose: Function __io_submit_one(ctx, iocb, user_iocb, req, compat) (aio.c:1969-2021). Precondition: req is an aio_kiocb obtained from aio_get_req (so req->ki_eventfd is NULL and req->ki_refcnt is 2), iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block, user_iocb its user address, compat selects the compat layout. Return statements and effects, in order: (1) req->ki_filp = fget(iocb->aio_fildes); if that is NULL it returns -EBADF (no file reference held). (2) If IOCB_FLAG_RESFD is set in aio_flags, eventfd_ctx_fdget(aio_resfd) is called; on an error pointer it returns PTR_ERR of it (req->ki_filp holds a file reference, req->ki_eventfd stays NULL); on success req->ki_eventfd is set. (3) If put_user(KIOCB_KEY, &user_iocb->aio_key) fails it returns -EFAULT (req->ki_filp, and req->ki_eventfd if it was set, hold references). (4) Otherwise req->ki_res.obj = user_iocb address, data = iocb->aio_data, res = 0, res2 = 0, and the function returns the result of the handler selected by iocb->aio_lio_opcode: IOCB_CMD_PREAD aio_read(non-vectored), PWRITE aio_write(non-vectored), PREADV aio_read(vectored), PWRITEV aio_write(vectored), FSYNC aio_fsync(datasync false), FDSYNC aio_fsync(datasync true), POLL aio_poll(req, iocb); any other opcode returns -EINVAL. Each of those handlers returns 0 or a negative errno: aio_read and aio_write return 0 when the I/O was started or completed (an -EIOCBQUEUED from the file operation is absorbed by aio_rw_done and not returned), aio_fsync returns 0 after scheduling the work, or -EINVAL or -ENOMEM, aio_poll returns 0 or -EINVAL. This function itself neither releases the file reference nor the eventfd reference and does not touch ki_refcnt; on a non-zero return the caller io_submit_one drops one reference with iocb_put(req) and then calls iocb_destroy(req) (which puts the eventfd if set, fput on ki_filp if set, drops the context reqs reference and frees req) and put_reqs_available(ctx, 1); when the return is 0 the caller still drops one reference with iocb_put(req) and the request is completed, or will be completed asynchronously, with the remaining reference. No lock is taken or held by this function.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:1969-2021 and the callees aio_read/aio_write/aio_fsync (aio.c:1581-1669), aio_rw_done (1561-1579), iocb_destroy (1103-1111), aio_get_req (1054-1073: refcount_set(...,2), ki_eventfd = NULL) and io_submit_one (2053-2066). Earlier prose claimed the function 'does not itself release' references and that handlers 'never' return -EIOCBQUEUED; the latter is now stated with its reason (absorbed in aio_rw_done, 1563-1565, and the handlers' return values come from rw_verify_area/aio_prep_rw, 1589-1605, 1616-1637). Added the caller's iocb_put on both success and failure paths (2056).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit, aio_context_t, ctx_id, long, nr,
prose: System call io_submit(ctx_id, nr, iocbpp) (aio.c:2082-2121). Precondition: iocbpp is a user pointer to an array of nr user pointers to struct iocb; the call may sleep. Return statements: three. (R1) -EINVAL if nr < 0, before any lookup. (R2) -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) returns NULL (no reference was taken). (R3) the final 'return i ? i : ret', reached only after a reference on the context (ctx->users) was obtained by lookup_ioctx. On that path: nr is first reduced to ctx->nr_events if it is larger; if the reduced nr is greater than AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD a block plug is started and finished around the loop. For i = 0 .. nr-1 the loop reads the i-th iocb pointer with get_user (on a fault ret = -EFAULT and the loop stops) and calls io_submit_one(ctx, user_iocb, false); a non-zero result is stored in ret and stops the loop (ret is unchanged and stays 0 for a successful call). When the loop stops at index i, i iocbs were submitted successfully; if it runs to the end, i == nr. Then the plug is finished if it was started, the ctx->users reference is dropped (percpu_ref_put, line 2119), and the function returns i if i > 0, otherwise ret, which is the error that stopped the first iteration (-EFAULT from reading the pointer, or the error of io_submit_one, for example -EFAULT, -EINVAL, -EAGAIN, -EBADF or an error of the I/O handler), or 0 if no iocb was attempted (nr == 0 after the reduction). An error that occurs after at least one successful submission is not reported; only the count is returned.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2082-2121. Three returns (2091, 2096, 2120); loop stop conditions (2107-2114); single reference drop at 2119. Previous prose said the reference is dropped 'on every path after the lookup', which is true but is now stated as the single path at 2119; also dropped the vague 'the first error' wording by naming that a later error after i > 0 is not reported (2120).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel, aio_context_t, ctx_id, struct iocb __user *, iocb,
prose: System call io_cancel(ctx_id, iocb, result) (aio.c:2176-2216). Precondition: iocb is a user pointer to a control block previously passed to io_submit; result is not used by the function. Return statements: four. (R1) -EFAULT if get_user of iocb->aio_key faults. (R2) -EINVAL if the key is not KIOCB_KEY. (R3) -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) returns NULL (no context reference taken). (R4) the final 'return ret' after a context reference was obtained. On that path ret starts as -EINVAL; under ctx->ctx_lock (irq-disabling) the function walks ctx->active_reqs for the first entry whose ki_res.obj equals the user address of iocb; if one is found it calls its ki_cancel callback with the embedded kiocb, stores the callback's return value in ret, removes the entry from the list with list_del_init, and stops the search; if none is found ret stays -EINVAL. The lock is released. If ret is 0 it is replaced by -EINPROGRESS (the completion event, if any, is delivered through the ring and not through result); any other value, including a negative value from the callback, is returned unchanged. The ctx->users reference is dropped before the return. Nothing is written to result.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2176-2216: four returns (2186, 2188, 2192, 2215); search and callback at 2194-2202; the 0 -> -EINPROGRESS conversion at 2204-2211; reference drop at 2213. The earlier prose said a callback return other than 0 'is returned unchanged' which holds, now with the explicit statement that nothing is written to result.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents, aio_context_t, ctx_id,
prose: System call io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (aio.c:2251-2267, built only with CONFIG_64BIT). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event; timeout is NULL (wait without a time limit) or a user pointer to a struct __kernel_timespec holding a relative timeout; the call may sleep. Return statements: two. (R1) -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_timespec64 returns non-zero (it returns -EFAULT when the copy from user fails). (R2) the final 'return ret'. On that path ret (an int) is the value of do_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, ts or NULL), except that when that value is 0 and signal_pending(current) is true ret becomes -EINTR. do_io_getevents returns -EINVAL if lookup_ioctx finds no context (including when reading the ring id from user space faults), or, once a context reference was taken, if min_nr < 0 or min_nr > nr; otherwise it returns read_events(...): the number of events copied to the user buffer (this may be 0 or fewer than min_nr when the timeout expires or a signal interrupts the wait, since neither condition is turned into an error by read_events), or a negative errno only when no event had been copied yet: -EFAULT if a copy to the user buffer faulted (in that read of the ring the head is not advanced, so events of that read that were already copied remain in the ring), or -EINVAL if the context is dead. The context reference taken by do_io_getevents is dropped before it returns. io_getevents takes no locks of its own.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2251-2267 and callees do_io_getevents (2218-2235), read_events (1312-1367), aio_read_events (1295-1310), aio_read_events_ring (1218-1293; fault path 1271-1277 skips the head update at 1284-1286), lookup_ioctx (1075-1100) and get_timespec64 (kernel/time/time.c:872-891). Removed the earlier claim 'it fails only when the copy from user faults' as a guess about callers; now stated as the get_timespec64 contract read from source (only -EFAULT). Clarified that the unconsumed events after a fault include those already copied in that same ring read (the head is advanced once after the loop).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents
prose: System call io_pgetevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig) (aio.c:2276-2307). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event; timeout is NULL or a user pointer to a struct __kernel_timespec (relative); usig is NULL or a user pointer to a struct __aio_sigset {sigmask, sigsetsize}; the call may sleep. Return statements: four. (R1) -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_timespec64 fails. (R2) -EFAULT if usig is non-NULL and copy_from_user of the sigset descriptor fails (a NULL usig leaves ksig = {NULL, 0}). (R3) the non-zero result of set_user_sigmask(ksig.sigmask, ksig.sigsetsize), returned before any wait: set_user_sigmask returns 0 without changing anything when the mask pointer is NULL, -EINVAL when sigsetsize is not sizeof(sigset_t), -EFAULT when the mask cannot be copied; only on its success with a non-NULL mask does it save the current blocked mask in saved_sigmask, set the restore flag and install the new mask. (R4) the final 'return ret'. On that path ret = do_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, ts or NULL) (events copied, or -EINVAL for an unknown context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a negative errno from the ring read when no event had been copied yet); then interrupted = signal_pending(current); restore_saved_sigmask_unless(interrupted) restores the saved signal mask if a mask was installed and no signal is pending (if a signal is pending the mask is left to be restored when the signal is delivered); if interrupted and ret is 0, ret becomes -ERESTARTNOHAND; otherwise ret is returned as it is. The only conversion of ret is 0 to -ERESTARTNOHAND when a signal is pending; unlike io_getevents there is no -EINTR conversion, and a non-zero ret is returned unchanged.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Re-derived from aio.c:2276-2307 and kernel/signal.c:3354-3370 (set_user_sigmask) and include/linux/sched/signal.h:571-577 (restore_saved_sigmask_unless). Four returns (2290, 2293, 2297, 2306). Earlier prose is kept in substance; added the exact set_user_sigmask contract (NULL mask returns 0) and the statement that no other conversion of ret happens.
