name: ceph_readdir
prose: Function ceph_readdir(file, ctx) (dir.c:317-639), the iterate_shared handler of a ceph directory. Precondition: file is an open directory whose private_data is its struct ceph_dir_file_info (dfi), ctx is a valid dir_context, no ceph spinlock is held by the caller. Return statements (all of them): (1) return 0 if CEPH_F_ATEND is set in dfi->file_info.flags. (2) return 0 if ctx->pos == 0 and dir_emit of '.' refuses; otherwise ctx->pos becomes 1. (3) return 0 if ctx->pos == 1 and dir_emit of '..' refuses; otherwise ctx->pos becomes 2. (4) return err if ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir(inode) returns a negative value (a non-negative return is ignored). (5) return err from __dcache_readdir, when the dcache path was taken and its result is not -EAGAIN. (6) return PTR_ERR(req) if ceph_mdsc_create_request fails. (7) return the error of ceph_alloc_readdir_reply_buffer after ceph_mdsc_put_request(req). (8) return -ENOMEM if kzalloc of r_path2 fails, after putting req. (9) return the negative result of ceph_encode_encrypted_dname, after putting req. (10) return the negative result of ceph_mdsc_do_request, after putting req. (11) return a non-zero result of note_last_dentry (-ENOMEM) after dropping dfi->last_readdir (put and set to NULL). (12) return -EIO, after dropping dfi->last_readdir (put and set to NULL), when a buffered entry has rde->offset < ctx->pos (dir.c:545-552). (13) return -EIO, after dropping dfi->last_readdir, when a buffered entry has no inode (rde->inode.in is NULL; 554-558). (14) return 0 when dir_emit refuses a buffered entry, with ctx->pos equal to that entry's offset and dfi->last_readdir kept (not put) so the next call resumes from it. (15) the final return 0. Behaviour. The dcache path (when the mount options have DCACHE and not NOASYNCREADDIR, the inode is not the snapshot dir, the directory is complete and ordered, and the shared file cap is issued) calls __dcache_readdir; only an -EAGAIN result falls through to the normal path. Before that, the write file mode is touched under i_ceph_lock. Normal path, label more: if need_send_readdir (no dfi->last_readdir, or the buffered frag does not cover ctx->pos) the old reply, if any, is put and set to NULL, a READDIR (or LSSNAP for the snapshot dir) request to the auth MDS is built for the frag (taken from ctx->pos, or chosen by ceph_choose_frag for hash order) with r_path2 holding the encoded last name when dfi->last_name is set, and sent; if the reply names another frag, dfi->frag is updated and, unless the reply is hash ordered, ctx->pos is set to the start of that frag. The reply is stored in dfi->last_readdir; the readdir-cache and dir_release_count bookkeeping is updated depending on CEPH_MDS_R_DID_PREPOPULATE; if the reply has entries note_last_dentry records the last name and the next offset (2 when dir_end), and if it has none but dir_end, next_offset = 2. Emission: a binary search over dir_entries (assuming ascending offsets) finds the first entry whose offset is >= ctx->pos, so entries with a smaller offset at the front of the buffer are skipped silently without error; for each entry from there on ctx->pos is set to the entry offset before dir_emit and incremented after a successful emit, and an entry whose offset is below the current ctx->pos (for example one that does not increase) makes the function return -EIO as listed in (12). When all buffered entries have been emitted the reply is put and dfi->last_readdir set to NULL; if dfi->next_offset > 2 the same frag is requested again (goto more); otherwise, if the frag is not the rightmost, the next frag is selected: for hash order ctx->pos is raised to the position of the next frag when that is larger, otherwise ctx->pos is set to the start of the next frag and dfi->last_name is freed and set to NULL; then goto more. At the end of the last frag CEPH_F_ATEND is set; if i_release_count equals dfi->dir_release_count, then under i_ceph_lock, if dfi->dir_ordered_count also equals i_ordered_count i_size is set to readdir_cache_idx * sizeof(struct dentry *) (a BUG_ON requires readdir_cache_idx >= 0 in that case), and in both cases __ceph_dir_set_complete(ci, dfi->dir_release_count, dfi->dir_ordered_count) records the directory as complete with those counts; then it returns 0. No ceph spinlock is held at any return. A reply kept in dfi->last_readdir stays there on returns (1) to (5) (they come before this call touches it) and on return (14); on returns (6) to (13) it has been put and set to NULL, or no reply was stored.
note: Reviewer claim (annotation says an offset below ctx->pos returns -EIO; code skips such entries): PARTLY RIGHT, but the -EIO behaviour is real. fs/ceph/dir.c:545-552: inside the emit loop 'if (rde->offset < ctx->pos) { pr_warn_client(...); ceph_mdsc_put_request(dfi->last_readdir); dfi->last_readdir = NULL; return -EIO; }'. What the reviewer saw as 'skip' is the binary search at 530-541 which advances i past leading entries with offset < ctx->pos before the loop starts, silently. So both behaviours exist: leading smaller entries are skipped (530-541), a smaller offset met inside the loop returns -EIO (545-552). The previous prose only said -EIO; the new prose states both. Other points verified from the source and fixed: complete marking always calls __ceph_dir_set_complete in both branches (632-633), only the ordered branch writes i_size (625-627); the full list of returns (333, 341, 355, 361, 378, 411, 416, 431, 438, 459, 515, 551, 557, 575, 638); the hash-order versus non-hash-order next-frag handling (593-604).

name: static inline void ecryptfs_release_messaging(void)
prose: This is the static inline stub ecryptfs_release_messaging(void) at ecryptfs_kernel.h:612-613, inside the #else branch (line 607) of '#ifdef CONFIG_ECRYPT_FS_MESSAGING' (line 598), so it is the definition seen only when CONFIG_ECRYPT_FS_MESSAGING is not defined. When that option is defined the header only declares 'void ecryptfs_release_messaging(void);' (line 606) and the real function is defined in messaging.c, which is not part of this item and is not described here. Precondition: none (the function has no parameters). Postcondition: the body is empty ('{ }'): it returns nothing, reads and writes no data, and takes or releases no lock, reference or memory. There is exactly one exit, the end of the empty body.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed). Checked against fs/ecryptfs/ecryptfs_kernel.h:598-612 (stub inside the #else branch, empty body) and fs/ecryptfs/messaging.c:420-455 (the real function, which frees the message context array, the daemon hash and destroys the miscdev; deliberately not attributed to the stub). The prose now states which configuration the stub belongs to and that the real function exists separately.

name: v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl
prose: The function in this item is v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl(dir, dentry, file, flags, omode) (vfs_inode_dotl.c:226-337), the atomic_open inode operation of 9P2000.L directories (the function named v9fs_vfs_create_dotl at line 220 is a different 3-line function that just returns v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(idmap, dir, dentry, omode, 0)). The slice starts at line 252, in the middle of it, so lines 242-250 are before the slice. Precondition: dir is a directory inode on a 9p mount, dentry names the entry to open in it, file is the struct file being opened, omode is the creation mode; the function may sleep. Result: an int; it returns 0 on success or a negative errno. Return statements: three. Before the slice start (lines 242-250): if d_in_lookup(dentry) is true the function calls v9fs_vfs_lookup(dir, dentry, 0); if that returns a non-NULL result or leaves the dentry positive, return 1 is finish_no_open(file, res) (line 245), which returns PTR_ERR(res) when res is an error pointer and otherwise stores res in file->f_path.dentry and returns 0; nothing is created. Return 2 (line 250): if flags does not have O_CREAT set, it returns finish_no_open(file, NULL), i.e. 0 with a NULL dentry stored in file, and nothing is created; there is no -ENOENT return and no finish_no_open(file, dentry) in this function. Return 3 (line 336), the common exit 'out', is reached with err = 0 or a negative errno after the creation steps in the slice, as follows. It takes v9ses from dir, then dfid = v9fs_parent_fid(dentry) (error: goto out), ofid = clone_fid(dfid) (error: goto out), gid = v9fs_get_fsgid_for_create(dir), mode = omode adjusted by v9fs_acl_mode (error: goto out; it also returns the default and access ACLs dacl and pacl), then, if the session has CACHE_WRITEBACK and p9_omode has P9_OWRITE, the write-only open is replaced by read-write without P9_DOTL_APPEND; then err = p9_client_create_dotl(ofid, name, p9_omode, mode, gid, &qid) (a negative result goes to out; from this point the file exists on the server even if a later step fails); v9fs_invalidate_inode_attr(dir); fid = p9_client_walk(dfid, 1, &name, 1) (error: goto out); inode = v9fs_get_new_inode_from_fid(v9ses, fid, dir->i_sb) (error: goto out, with fid still owned here); v9fs_set_create_acl(inode, fid, dacl, pacl); v9fs_fid_add(dentry, &fid) hands fid to the dentry and sets the local fid to NULL; d_instantiate(dentry, inode); err = finish_open(file, dentry, generic_file_open) (a non-zero result goes to out, after the dentry has already been instantiated with the new inode). On success it sets file->private_data = ofid, with CONFIG_9P_FSCACHE and CACHE_FSCACHE calls fscache_use_cookie for the inode's cookie, calls v9fs_fid_add_modes(ofid, ...), v9fs_open_fid_add(inode, &ofid) (adds ofid to the inode's open-fid list and sets the local ofid to NULL), and sets FMODE_CREATED in file->f_mode. At out, p9_fid_put is called on dfid, ofid and fid (each call is a no-op for a NULL or error pointer; a fid handed over above is already NULL), v9fs_put_acl(dacl, pacl) releases the ACL references, and err is returned. dfid is not handed over to anything, so it is dropped at out; ofid and fid are dropped there only if they were not handed over (a handed-over one is NULL).
note: Reviewer claim (prose says O_CREAT unset returns finish_no_open(file, NULL); code returns -ENOENT or finish_no_open(file, dentry)): WRONG. fs/9p/vfs_inode_dotl.c:249-250 reads 'if (!(flags & O_CREAT)) return finish_no_open(file, NULL);' and there is no -ENOENT in the function (the only returns are 245, 250, 336). The reviewer was working from the slice that starts at line 252, which does not contain lines 242-250 at all; the prose now says explicitly that lines 242-250 precede the slice and quotes them. Other fixes: finish_no_open (fs/open.c:1072-1078) returns PTR_ERR(dentry) for an error pointer, so the first return is 'finish_no_open(file, res)' and not simply 0; p9_fid_put ignores NULL and error pointers (include/net/9p/client.h:269-272); v9fs_fid_add and v9fs_open_fid_add set the caller's pointer to NULL (fs/9p/fid.c:33-42, 93-102). The dentry is instantiated at 313-314, before finish_open at 317, so only a finish_open failure leaves an instantiated dentry.

name: resolve_indirect_refs
prose: Function resolve_indirect_refs(ctx, path, preftrees, sc) (backref.c:730-830). Precondition: ctx, path and preftrees are valid; preftrees->indirect is expected to hold only refs without ref->parent set (a ref with ref->parent set is detected and rejected, see below); sc is NULL or a share-check context. Return statements: two. (R1) -ENOMEM if ulist_alloc(GFP_NOFS) for the local parents ulist fails; no other step has run. (R2) the final return ret after label out, which first calls free_leaf_list(parents), reached from all the other exits described below. The loop runs while the indirect tree is non-empty; each pass takes the first ref in the tree (rb_first_cached). (a) If that ref has ref->parent non-zero, WARN fires, ret = -EINVAL and the function goes to out; the ref stays in the indirect tree. Otherwise the ref is erased from the indirect tree and the indirect count is decremented, so from here on this pass owns it. (b) If ref->count == 0 the ref is freed (free_pref) and the loop continues. (c) If sc is non-NULL and ref->root_id differs from btrfs_root_id(sc->root), the ref is freed, ret = BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED (6, positive) and the function goes to out. (d) Otherwise ret2 = resolve_indirect_ref(ctx, path, preftrees, ref, parents). If ret2 == -ENOENT the ref is inserted unchanged into the direct tree with prelim_ref_insert (which may merge it into an equal existing ref and free it) and the loop continues without calling ulist_reinit on parents. If ret2 is any other non-zero value (a negative errno or the positive value 1) the ref is freed, ret = ret2 and the function goes to out. (e) If ret2 == 0: the first node of the parents ulist, if any, supplies the ref's parent (node->val, or 0 when the ulist is empty) and the ref's inode_list (the node's aux list, or NULL). For each further node of parents a new prelim_ref is allocated (GFP_NOFS); if that allocation fails the current ref is freed, ret = -ENOMEM and the function goes to out; otherwise the new ref is a memcpy of the current ref with its own parent (node->val) and inode_list (the node's aux list) and is inserted into the direct tree with prelim_ref_insert (which may merge it and free it). So the original ref is reused for the first parent and a new ref is allocated only for each additional parent. After that the original ref itself is inserted into the direct tree last, with prelim_ref_insert (it may be merged into an equal ref and freed there); then ulist_reinit(parents) (which frees the nodes but not the inode lists, which now belong to the refs) and cond_resched, and the loop continues. When the indirect tree is empty the loop ends with ret == 0 and the function returns 0 after out. At out, free_leaf_list(parents) frees the inode element list attached to every node still in the parents ulist and then frees the ulist. On the -ENOMEM path of (e) the parents ulist still holds all nodes of this pass, so it also frees lists that had already been attached to the current ref (which is freed) and to new refs already inserted into the direct tree in this pass; those refs, if still in the direct tree, still point to the freed lists. On an early return the refs not yet taken stay in the indirect tree; a ref taken by the failing pass is either freed (cases b, c, d-error, e-ENOMEM) or was inserted into the direct tree.
note: Reviewer claim (code allocates a new ref for every parent and frees the original; annotation says the original ref is reused/inserted): WRONG. fs/btrfs/backref.c:790-794 puts the first parent into the existing ref ('ref->parent = node ? node->val : 0; ref->inode_list = unode_aux_to_inode_list(node);'); only the loop at 797-812 allocates a new_ref, and that is for each further parent (the iterator has already consumed the first node at 792); the original ref is inserted at 818 ('we must do this last because the ref could be merged/freed here'). The original is freed only on the error paths (766, 771, 785, 803) or inside prelim_ref_insert when it merges (backref.c:300-323). Also checked and stated: -ENOENT path does not reinitialise parents (780-783 'continue' skips 820), the single positive return value 6 (backref.c:25), the two returns (743, 829).

name: cow_file_range
prose: Function cow_file_range(inode, locked_folio, start, end, done_offset, flags) (inode.c:1287-1563; the slice begins at its first statement, line 1307). Precondition: [start, end] (end inclusive) is a delalloc range of the inode with its data space reserved; locked_folio is NULL or the locked folio of the range; done_offset is NULL or points to a u64; flags is a combination of COW_FILE_RANGE_* (NO_INLINE, KEEP_LOCKED); the range length rounded up to the sector size (at least one sector) is expected not to exceed the filesystem total bytes (checked only by ASSERT). Return statements: two, both 'return ret'. (R1) at label done (line 1483): reached by 'goto done' after the inline step, and by falling out of the loop; it first stores *done_offset = end when done_offset is non-NULL. (R2) at the end of the error cleanup (line 1562), after a btrfs_err message; the error path does not write *done_offset. Steps. (1) If the inode is a free-space inode, ret = -EINVAL and control goes to out_unlock (nothing has been reserved: cur_alloc_size is 0 and start is orig_start, so only the third region below is cleaned up). (2) num_bytes = the length rounded up to the sector size (at least one sector); inode_should_defrag(inode, start, end, num_bytes, SZ_64K) is called. (3) Unless COW_FILE_RANGE_NO_INLINE is set, ret = cow_file_range_inline(...): ret == 0 becomes 1 and ret < 0 stays negative, both going to done (so a negative inline error is returned with *done_offset = end written when done_offset is non-NULL; cow_file_range_inline has already cleaned up in both cases); ret > 0 (inline not possible) continues with the normal path. (4) alloc_hint is taken from btrfs_get_extent_allocation_hint; page_ops = PAGE_SET_ORDERED, plus PAGE_UNLOCK unless COW_FILE_RANGE_KEEP_LOCKED; min_alloc_size is num_bytes for a data relocation root, otherwise the sector size. (5) The loop runs while num_bytes > 0. It calls btrfs_reserve_extent for num_bytes with min_alloc_size. On -EAGAIN (zoned only): if start == orig_start it waits for BTRFS_FS_NEED_ZONE_FINISH and retries the iteration; otherwise if done_offset is non-NULL it sets end = start - 1, ret = 0 and leaves the loop; otherwise ret = -ENOSPC. Any negative ret then goes to out_unlock. With an extent reserved (cur_alloc_size = ins.offset) it locks the extent range [start, start + cur_alloc_size - 1], creates the io extent map (failure: unlock that range, ret = PTR_ERR, goto out_reserve), allocates the ordered extent (failure: unlock that range, ret = PTR_ERR, goto out_drop_extent_cache), and for a data relocation root calls btrfs_reloc_clone_csums(ordered) (failure: drops the extent map range of this extent, ret kept). It then puts the ordered extent reference, calls btrfs_dec_block_group_reservations, reduces num_bytes (to 0 if the extent was larger), sets alloc_hint, advances start by cur_alloc_size and resets cur_alloc_size to 0; if ret is non-zero (only possible after the csums failure) it goes to out_unlock, with the reserved extent not freed here because it belongs to the ordered extent. (6) After the loop, extent_clear_unlock_delalloc(orig_start, end) clears EXTENT_LOCKED and EXTENT_DELALLOC over [orig_start, end] and applies page_ops to the folios (end may have been shortened in the zoned case), then done: and R1 with ret == 0 (or 1 from the inline step). Error cleanup. Label out_drop_extent_cache drops the extent map range [start, start + cur_alloc_size - 1] and falls into out_reserve, which calls btrfs_dec_block_group_reservations and btrfs_free_reserved_extent(ins.objectid, ins.offset) and falls into out_unlock. At out_unlock three regions are handled in this order. Region 1, [orig_start, start - 1], only if orig_start < start: if locked_folio is NULL, mapping_set_error(mapping, ret); btrfs_cleanup_ordered_extents(inode, orig_start, start - orig_start); then extent_clear_unlock_delalloc clears only EXTENT_LOCKED and EXTENT_DELALLOC there (the other bits are handled by the ordered extent cleanup) and applies PAGE_UNLOCK | PAGE_START_WRITEBACK | PAGE_END_WRITEBACK. Region 2, [start, start + cur_alloc_size - 1], only if cur_alloc_size is non-zero: extent_clear_unlock_delalloc clears EXTENT_LOCKED | EXTENT_DELALLOC | EXTENT_DELALLOC_NEW | EXTENT_DEFRAG | EXTENT_CLEAR_META_RESV (not EXTENT_CLEAR_DATA_RESV) with the same page_ops, and btrfs_qgroup_free_data releases its data qgroup reservation. Region 3, [start + cur_alloc_size, end], only if start + cur_alloc_size < end: the same bits plus EXTENT_CLEAR_DATA_RESV are cleared with the same page_ops, and btrfs_qgroup_free_data releases its data qgroup reservation. Then btrfs_err logs the failure and the function returns the negative ret (R2). Which regions are processed depends on the failing step. Free-space inode: only region 3, which is then the whole range. btrfs_reserve_extent failure (or the -ENOSPC conversion): region 3 is the range from start to end, and region 1 is processed only if earlier extents were already handled (orig_start < start); region 2 is skipped because cur_alloc_size is 0. io extent map or ordered extent allocation failure: region 2 is the current extent, region 3 the rest, and region 1 only if earlier extents were handled. btrfs_reloc_clone_csums failure: start was already advanced and cur_alloc_size reset to 0, so region 1 (now including the current extent) and region 3 are processed and region 2 is skipped.
note: Reviewer claim (cleanup also clears DELALLOC_NEW/DEFRAG/META_RESV, not only delalloc/lock bits): RIGHT for regions 2 and 3 and for the free-space-inode path. fs/btrfs/inode.c:1521-1522 sets clear_bits = EXTENT_LOCKED | EXTENT_DELALLOC | EXTENT_DELALLOC_NEW | EXTENT_DEFRAG | EXTENT_CLEAR_META_RESV, used by the region-2 call at 1536-1539 and (with EXTENT_CLEAR_DATA_RESV added at 1550) by the region-3 call at 1551-1553; only region 1 (1509-1519) clears just LOCKED|DELALLOC, with the comment at 1503-1506 explaining why. The previous prose said the free-space-inode path clears only 'delalloc/lock bits': wrong (1307-1310 goes to out_unlock, whose region 3 uses the full set). Other real errors fixed: (a) the previous prose claimed the error path 'never writes *done_offset' without noting that the inline-error path (1322-1332) goes to done and does write it (1481-1482); (b) the precondition 'extent bits locked by the caller' is not supported by the code (the function itself locks each reserved range at 1417-1418 and cow_file_range_inline locks at 706); removed. Checked returns (1483, 1562), labels 1480-1563 and cow_file_range_inline's return contract (inode.c:703-735: 1 not possible, 0 done and cleaned up, <0 error already cleaned up, >0 from the helper unlocks and returns it).

name: ext4_ext_insert_extent
prose: The function in this item is ext4_ext_insert_extent(handle, inode, path, newext, gb_flags) (extents.c:1997-2221); the slice starts at line 2046, in the middle of it (the text '(tail; name elided in excerpt)' is not part of the name; the lines before the slice, 1997-2045, hold the argument checks and the PRE_IO guard described below). Precondition: handle is an active journal handle with enough credits; path is the extent-tree path from ext4_find_extent for newext's logical block, valid down to the leaf at ext_depth(inode); newext points to the extent to insert, whose block range does not overlap an existing extent; gb_flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags. Result: a struct ext4_ext_path pointer, or an error pointer. Return statements: three. (R1) 'return path' at 2140 when ext4_ext_create_new_leaf returns an error pointer. (R2) 'return path' at 2216 on success. (R3) 'return ERR_PTR(err)' at 2220, after errout frees the current path, the one passed in or its replacement (ext4_free_ext_path). The function behaves as follows. Before the slice: if gb_flags has DELALLOC_RESERVE, mb_flags gets EXT4_MB_DELALLOC_RESERVED; if the actual length of newext is 0, EXT4_ERROR_INODE is reported and err = -EFSCORRUPTED goes to errout; if path[depth].p_hdr is NULL, -EFSCORRUPTED goes to errout. Then, at line 2025, 'if (ex && !(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO))' guards the whole neighbour-merge block (the lines in this slice from 2046 on up to 2096 are inside it): when gb_flags has EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO, or when there is no nearest extent ex, this block is skipped entirely, i.e. neither the append nor the prepend merge is tried. Inside the block (the part visible in this slice from 2046): ex is first moved to its right neighbour (when it is not the last extent and ends before newext, then 'goto prepend') or left neighbour (when it is not the first extent and newext ends before it); then, if ext4_can_extents_be_merged(inode, ex, newext), the extent is appended: ext4_ext_get_access (error: errout), ex->ee_len grows by newext's length keeping the unwritten mark, nearex = ex, goto merge; else at prepend:, if ext4_can_extents_be_merged(inode, newext, ex), ext4_ext_get_access (error: errout), ex takes newext's block and physical block and grows by newext's length keeping the unwritten mark, nearex = ex, goto merge. If no merge was done or the block was skipped: depth and eh are re-read; if the leaf has room (eh_entries < eh_max) goto has_space. Otherwise the next leaf is tried when newext's block is above the last extent of this leaf and ext4_ext_next_leaf_block gives a block: ext4_find_extent(inode, next, NULL, gb_flags) (error: err goes to errout), BUG_ON on a depth mismatch, and if that leaf has room the old path is freed (ext4_free_ext_path) and the new path replaces it (goto has_space), else the new path is freed. If still no room: with gb_flags METADATA_NOFAIL mb_flags gets EXT4_MB_USE_RESERVED, and path = ext4_ext_create_new_leaf(...) (an error pointer is returned directly as R1; that function frees the path itself on failure); depth and eh are re-read. has_space: nearex = path[depth].p_ext; ext4_ext_get_access (error: errout); with no extent in the leaf nearex is the first slot; otherwise nearex is advanced by one if newext's block is above nearex's block (BUG_ON equal blocks otherwise) and the entries from there to the end of the leaf are moved up by one slot with memmove; eh_entries is incremented, path[depth].p_ext = nearex and the block, physical block and length of newext are stored in it. merge: when gb_flags does not have PRE_IO, ext4_ext_try_to_merge(handle, inode, path, nearex) is called (no result); then ext4_ext_correct_indexes (error: errout) and ext4_ext_dirty on path + path->p_depth (error: errout); then R2. With gb_flags PRE_IO therefore both the append/prepend merge (line 2025) and ext4_ext_try_to_merge (line 2204) are skipped. On success the returned path is the one passed in or, if the next leaf or a new leaf was used, a different path that replaces it; the caller owns the returned path. On an error return the caller gets only the error pointer and must not use the path it passed in, because it was freed by this function, or by ext4_ext_create_new_leaf or ext4_find_extent on their failures. When a late step (index correction or dirtying) fails, the in-memory leaf may already contain the change.
note: Reviewer claim (PRE_IO does not skip append/prepend merging; only ext4_ext_try_to_merge is skipped): WRONG. fs/ext4/extents.c:2025 'if (ex && !(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO)) {' opens the block that contains both the append attempt (2047-2067) and the prepend attempt (2069-2095) and closes at 2096, so with PRE_IO neither is tried; and 2204 'if (!(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO)) ext4_ext_try_to_merge(...)' separately skips the post-insert merge. The slice given to the reviewer begins at line 2046, after the guard at 2025, so the guard was not visible; the prose now states the guard with its line number. Other points verified: three returns (2140, 2216, 2220); ext4_ext_create_new_leaf frees the path on its own failures (extents.c:1460-1462 and ext4_find_extent's err label at 970-972); the early errors -EFSCORRUPTED at 2010-2013 and 2018-2022 are before the slice.

name: afs_select_vlserver
prose: Function afs_select_vlserver(vc) (vl_rotate.c:93-319): selects the next volume location server and address to try, and may be called repeatedly. Precondition: vc was set up by afs_begin_vlserver_operation (nr_iterations starts at -1); on calls after the first, vc->alist is the address list used by the previous call, vc->addr_index indexes the address tried, and vc->call_error, vc->call_abort_code and vc->call_responded hold the outcome of the previous call; the cursor is used by one task at a time. Return statements: four. (R1) return false at line 111 if AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is already set. (R2) return false at line 127 when the previous call's error is 0 or any error not listed below. (R3) return true at line 278 when an address has been selected. (R4) return false at line 318, the end of label failed. In every case vc->nr_iterations is incremented first (line 102), before the STOP test. Control flow. (R1): no other change. First call (nr_iterations == 0 after the increment): goto start. Later calls: last_error of alist->addrs[vc->addr_index] is set to call_error, then call_error selects: 0 or any unlisted error: cumul_error.error = error, AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is set, R2; the alist and server_list references stay in the cursor. -ECONNABORTED: with abort code AFSVL_IO, AFSVL_BADVOLOPER or AFSVL_NOMEM, afs_prioritise_error(cumul_error, -EREMOTEIO, abort_code) and goto next_server; with any other abort code, afs_prioritise_error(cumul_error, error, abort_code) and goto failed. -ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME: afs_prioritise_error(cumul_error, error, 0) and goto iterate_address. -ECONNRESET: the same recording, AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY is set, goto next_server. -EOPNOTSUPP: goto next_server with no error recorded. Label next_server: if vc->call_responded, vc->addr_index != alist->preferred and the bit alist->preferred is set in vc->addr_tried, alist->preferred is set to vc->addr_index; the alist reference is put (afs_put_addrlist) and both alist and vc->alist become NULL; then pick_server. Label restart_from_beginning (reached only from no_more_servers when RETRY is set): it tests vc->call_responded and, when that is true, evaluates vc->alist->preferred although vc->alist is NULL on the only path that reaches this label, from no_more_servers (it was cleared at next_server before pick_server), so with call_responded true this line dereferences a NULL pointer; when call_responded is false, afs_put_addrlist(NULL) does nothing; the server list reference is put and vc->server_list set to NULL; if AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRIED is already set goto failed, else RETRIED is set and control falls into start. Label start: afs_start_vl_iteration(vc); if it returns false goto failed. That function may wait interruptibly for a DNS lookup (a signal sets cumul_error.error = -ERESTARTSYS), sets -ENOENT if DNS reports the cell as not found, -EDESTADDRREQ if no DNS record is available, and otherwise takes a reference on the cell's server list into vc->server_list; if that list has no servers it returns false without setting an error (the reference stays held), else it sets untried_servers to one bit per server and server_index = -1. Then afs_send_vl_probes (an error < 0 is recorded with afs_prioritise_error and goes to failed), then pick_server. Label pick_server: afs_wait_for_vl_probes (an error < 0 is recorded and goes to failed); server_index = server_list->preferred; if that bit is still set in untried_servers goto selected_server (the preferred server is chosen without checking that it responded); otherwise the untried server with AFS_VLSERVER_FL_RESPONDING set and the lowest probe rtt is chosen, the last one among equal rtts; if none exists goto no_more_servers. Label selected_server: its bit is cleared in untried_servers, vc->server is set, the server's address list is read under its lock and a reference taken into vc->alist, vc->addr_tried = 0, vc->addr_index = -1, falling into iterate_address. Label iterate_address: the candidate set is alist->responded minus alist->probe_failed minus vc->addr_tried; if it is empty goto next_server; vc->addr_index is alist->preferred if that bit is in the set, else the lowest set bit; that bit is set in vc->addr_tried, vc->alist = alist, vc->call_responded = false, and R3 returns true. Label no_more_servers: if AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY is set goto restart_from_beginning; otherwise for each server in the list cumul_error.responded is set when it is RESPONDING and its probe error and abort code are merged with afs_prioritise_error, then fall into failed. Label failed: if alist is non-NULL the preferred address is updated as in next_server, the reference is put and alist and vc->alist become NULL; AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is set and R4 returns false; vc->server_list stays referenced (it is NULL only after restart_from_beginning put it and start did not reload it) for afs_end_vlserver_operation, and the final error is in vc->cumul_error.
note: Previously unreviewed (review call failed), prose rebuilt from the full control flow of fs/afs/vl_rotate.c:93-319 plus afs_start_vl_iteration (42-87). Four returns (111, 127, 278, 318); eight labels. Corrections to the earlier text: (1) the earlier prose said the preferred-address update happens when 'the last call responded on a different address whose preferred address was tried'; the code tests call_responded, addr_index != alist->preferred, and the preferred bit in addr_tried (283-286, 309-312, 174-177); (2) the earlier prose omitted that the preferred server is picked without a responding check (210-212); (3) restart_from_beginning (172-185) reads vc->alist->preferred when vc->call_responded is true although vc->alist was set to NULL at 288 before pick_server (the only path in is no_more_servers at 295-296); this is an apparent NULL dereference in the source and is stated as such, not hidden; call_responded is set from the call outcome in fs/afs/vlclient.c:155, 304, 667, 785, so it can be true; (4) after the first-call 'start' path the server_list reference is held on every false return that follows afs_start_vl_iteration taking it (including the empty-list case, 81-82).

name: de_thread
prose: Function de_thread(tsk) (exec.c:912-1045): during exec, makes tsk the only thread of its thread group and the group leader. Precondition: tsk is current, in the middle of an exec; tsk->signal and tsk->sighand are valid; the caller holds neither siglock nor tasklist_lock; the function may sleep. Result: 0 on success, -EAGAIN if the exec cannot proceed. Return statements: three. (R1) return -EAGAIN at line 931. (R2) return 0 at line 1036. (R3) return -EAGAIN at line 1044 (label killed). Control flow. (a) If thread_group_empty(tsk), goto no_thread_group: tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD, BUG_ON(tsk is not the group leader), then R2; sig->group_exec_task and sig->notify_count are not touched on this path. (b) Otherwise siglock (spin_lock_irq on oldsighand->siglock) is taken; if SIGNAL_GROUP_EXIT is set in sig->flags or sig->group_exec_task is non-NULL, siglock is released and R1 is returned with no state changed. (c) Otherwise sig->group_exec_task = tsk and sig->notify_count = zap_other_threads(tsk), decremented by one if tsk is not the group leader. While notify_count is non-zero: the task state is set to TASK_KILLABLE, siglock is released, schedule() is called, and if a fatal signal is pending the function jumps to killed (with siglock not held); otherwise siglock is retaken. When notify_count is 0 siglock is released. (d) If tsk is not the group leader, it waits for the old leader to exit: in a loop it calls cgroup_threadgroup_change_begin(tsk), takes tasklist_lock for writing (write_lock_irq), sets sig->notify_count = -1 under that lock, and if leader->exit_state is non-zero leaves the loop still holding both; otherwise it sets TASK_KILLABLE, releases tasklist_lock and the cgroup threadgroup change, calls schedule(), and jumps to killed if a fatal signal is pending (holding neither lock). After leaving the loop, still holding tasklist_lock (write) and the cgroup threadgroup lock: tsk takes the leader's start_time and start_boottime, BUG_ON(leader and tsk are not in the same thread group), exchange_tids(tsk, leader), transfer_pid of the leader's TGID, PGID and SID pids to tsk, list_replace_rcu of the leader's tasks entry and list_replace_init of its sibling entry by tsk's, tsk->group_leader = leader->group_leader = tsk, tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD and leader->exit_signal = -1, BUG_ON(leader->exit_state != EXIT_ZOMBIE), leader->exit_state = EXIT_DEAD, __wake_up_parent(leader, leader->parent) if the leader is ptraced; then tasklist_lock and the threadgroup change are released and release_task(leader) is called after that. (e) For both the leader and non-leader callers that reached this point, sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0 are written without holding siglock or tasklist_lock, then control falls into no_thread_group: tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD, BUG_ON(tsk is not the group leader), R2 returns 0. (f) Label killed (reached only from the two killable waits above): read_lock(&tasklist_lock) is taken, sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0 are written, tasklist_lock is released, and R3 returns -EAGAIN; other threads may already have been killed and are not revived. siglock is not taken in the killed path; the siglock-protected region of (b)/(c) ends before any wait.
note: Reviewer claim (killed path uses siglock, not tasklist_lock, to reset group_exec_task/notify_count): WRONG. fs/exec.c:1038-1044 reads 'killed: /* protects against exit_notify() and __exit_signal() */ read_lock(&tasklist_lock); sig->group_exec_task = NULL; sig->notify_count = 0; read_unlock(&tasklist_lock); return -EAGAIN;'. siglock is released at 930/941 before the waits, and is not taken on the killed path. The previous prose said tasklist_lock for reading, which is correct and is kept. Other checks: three returns (931, 1036, 1044); the success-path reset at 1028-1029 is unlocked; notify_count = -1 is set under tasklist_lock (964); release_task(leader) is called after both locks are dropped (1022-1025).
